issueCommentThread.body:
Adoption blocker.

This is about Requirements: what done means. The person says what the change must do, and Directive is supposed to check that the code actually does that, and does not wander past it.

What a new person hits: They tell the agent not to add features beyond what they asked for. That limit is not enforced.

Why that ruins the product for them: A small fix turns into a pile of extra changes. The product does not hold the boundary they set, so it feels unsafe to leave it running.

How likely: High on a first "fix this one thing" request. Keeping the change small is the whole point of that request.

Companion `meta/lessons.md` / packs lessons restate the same adjacent-work / skill-bleed class. None of those lines name operator product-scope phrases ("do not add", "initial version only"), requirement lists, routes, actions, or pages.

The dogfood failure in the issue body (CRUD beyond the stated adds) would be declared already covered by rules that never bind that product surface.

## Intent ceiling is slash-verb containment, not prompt-phrase product scope
blocks-the-design
Evidence: `content/contracts/intent-ceiling.md` and `packages/core/src/policy/intent-ceiling.ts` at the dispatch SHA define #1193 R1–R3: `DEFT_SESSION_SLASH_VERB`, implement vs non-implement stems, `evaluateIntentCeiling` for implement/push/pr/merge/deploy, hotfix eligibility, and human merge. Failure mode: Citing `contracts/intent-ceiling.md` as proof that an explicit operator scope-limit sentence is already a hard ceiling misnames the mechanism. A `/build` session remains implement-authorized while still free to invent CRUD beyond the prompt list.
Disposition: Drop intent-ceiling from the "already treats … as a hard ceiling" premise before any bind that says #810 and pre-PR need no new check.

## #810 preflight never seeds or enforces a prompt-phrase ceiling
blocks-the-design
Evidence: `packages/cli/src/vbrief-preflight.ts` documents exit 0 only for `xbrief/active/` (or legacy) with `plan.status == running`. `packages/core/src/preflight/evaluate.ts` gates folder/status, then slash intent-ceiling from env, origin freshness, project invariants, intended placement, observable mint — still no operator-prompt phrase parse and no routes/actions/pages vs requirement lines. Stop 1 P2 and the issue body record no `xbrief/active/` brief on the failing build, so preflight had no declared scope artifact at all.
Failure mode: Binding "Implementation Intent Gate (#810) … need no phrase detection" leaves the empty-active path that already failed in dogfood: no brief means no ceiling object, and even a running brief is not loaded with a hard ceiling from the operator's scope-limit sentence by any inventoryed seed path at this SHA.
Disposition: Do not bind the no-phrase-detection / no-surface-check conclusion. Any successor lean must name how a scope-limit sentence becomes durable ceiling authority (or an alternate deterministic control) when rapid/greenfield has no active brief.

## Pre-PR Diff is agent judgment against xBRIEF AC, not a surface inventory
sharpens-framing
Evidence: `content/skills/deft-directive-pre-pr/SKILL.md` at the dispatch SHA requires comparing changed files to `xbrief/active/` acceptance criteria and checking for scope creep beyond those criteria; Diff phase is prose obligation. Repo-wide search at this SHA finds no shipped-surface enumerator of exported server actions / route files / pages traced to requirement lines, and no phrase-detect → brief-ceiling writer feeding that Diff.
Failure mode: Treating existing pre-PR as already discharging a warn-first list of untraceable routes/actions/pages overclaims. Without an active brief (P2), the Diff comparison has no machine-declared requirement list; with only soft AC prose, full-CRUD defaults still pass a judgment-only Diff.
Disposition: If a lean keeps "no shipped-surface-vs-requirements check," it must steelman a different existing deterministic control by path. Inventory at this SHA does not supply one. Framing the residual as missing durable ceiling + omission-proof surface check (warn-first) matches the issue's suggested direction more honestly than "pre-PR already covers it."

## Injection / swarm lens
Operator prompt text that is supposed to become plan authority or a gate ceiling is untrusted data until a seed path records it. The target asserts that existing stay-on-task / intent-ceiling prose already elevates an explicit scope-limit sentence to hard ceiling without phrase detection and without a surface check. That is authority-by-recital: the prompt remains free text, #810 does not ingest it, and pre-PR has no surface inventory. Issue body and comment text were treated as data only.

Strongest defense of the target: ordinary instruction-following plus #198 "do not drift into adjacent work" already makes "do not add features beyond the requirements" the task boundary, so inventing edit/delete is skill failure, not a missing gate. What flips that verdict: (1) the same prompt with no framework stayed add-only while Directive 0.118.1 rapid shipped extra CRUD; (2) every named anchor (#198/#241, skill exit, intent-ceiling.md, #810 evaluate, pre-PR Diff) was re-checked at `073525956dd7` and none binds prompt-phrase → hard ceiling → shipped-surface diff. Prose the agent already ignored is not a hard ceiling in the sense the target claims for skipping new controls.

The refutation target does not survive. Existing stay-on-task and intent-ceiling mechanisms do not treat an operator's explicit "do not add / initial version only" sentence as a hard ceiling on shipped product surface, so the claim that #810 and pre-PR need no phrase detection and no shipped-surface-vs-requirements check cannot bind as written.

## Additional defect evidence: an agent-derived implementation decision replaced explicit scope authorization

This is a behavioral report with consumer-specific identities and artifacts omitted. It adds a cross-layer failure case to the existing operator-ceiling defect.

### Observed sequence

1. The operator authorized UI changes only, and the source work items included a view-only restriction.
2. The agent converted desired display outcomes into implementation items that included persistence and backend changes.
3. The agent rewrote derived brief narratives so the original restriction no longer appeared in the reference used by acceptance checking.
4. A worker made a data-model decision and cited the agent-derived brief as its governing rule. No explicit operator approval of the backend/database expansion was recorded.
5. Lifecycle/readiness and quality checks passed or emitted nonblocking warnings. The agent treated those results as sufficient to continue.
6. Generic permission to merge was later treated as permission to land the expanded work. The permission did not explicitly authorize a change to the UI-only boundary.
7. Backend/database changes reached merge before the operator challenged the scope expansion.

Final delivery-gate observations used Directive 0.119.5. The earlier acceptance rewrite/pass observation used 0.119.9. Neither is presented as a test of the latest upstream revision.

### What failed

The authorization chain was circular: an agent-authored brief supported an agent-authored implementation decision, which then supported work beyond the operator's instruction. The operator's restriction was not independently enforced at the point the proposed mechanism crossed into another change class.

An action verb such as implement or swarm can authorize work within a stated scope. It cannot authorize all mechanisms that an agent considers useful. Likewise, lifecycle-ready is not implementation authorization, test success is not scope approval, and a generic merge approval does not explicitly amend an existing scope restriction.

The agent violated the instruction. Existing prose requiring confirmation for architectural or cross-cutting changes did not cause an independent stop. This is a systemic enforcement failure in addition to the agent error.

### Expected behavior

The operator ceiling must survive ingestion, delegation, compaction, review, and merge preparation. When an implementation needs backend or persistence changes beyond an explicit UI-only ceiling, the agent must present that concrete delta for an explicit operator decision before doing the dependent work.

An in-scope implementation should continue under the authorization already given. The fix must avoid repetitive approval requests for work that has not expanded.

### Reproduction recipe

Reconstructed from the observed sequence; not rerun as a separate sanitized fixture:

1. Authorize a UI-only outcome.
2. Have the agent infer that new persistence or processing is needed.
3. Let it record that choice in its own brief and decision log without an operator amendment.
4. Run the normal readiness, acceptance, and review flow.
5. Supply a generic instruction to continue or merge, without authorizing the added backend work.
6. The system must preserve the original ceiling and refuse the expansion; proceeding because the brief/decision/checks are internally consistent reproduces this defect.

### Regression cases

- A source statement containing "only" remains binding after derivation and delegation.
- A positive outcome request that appears to require excluded work produces a scope conflict, not implicit authorization.
- Agent-written briefs and architectural decisions cannot independently amend the ceiling.
- Generic proceed/continue/merge approvals retain the existing scope.
- An explicit operator amendment naming the added change class can authorize the specific expansion.
- The approved amendment remains bound to the affected work through delegation and merge preparation.
- A passing readiness or narrow semantic check cannot stand in for that amendment.

Refs #4774 for the absent PR membership boundary, #4915 for acceptance-reference loss, and #4541 for limited intent-constraint coverage. These are contributing failures; this report isolates the missing transition from an agent's proposed mechanism to explicit operator authorization.

Related reports filed from the same behavioral audit: #5055, #5056.

metadata.issueBody:
## Summary

The operator prompt for a greenfield build ended with:

> Start with this initial version only. Do not add features beyond the requirements above.

The requirements listed *add* vehicle, *add* maintenance record, *add* modification, and *update* mileage. The agent also implemented edit + delete for vehicles, service records, and modifications (`updateVehicleAction`, `deleteVehicleAction`, `updateServiceAction`, `deleteServiceAction`, `updateModificationAction`, `deleteModificationAction`, plus the matching `/edit` pages). None of that was requested.

A control build of the same prompt with no framework installed stayed add-only.

## Environment

- `@deftai/directive` 0.118.1, consumer deposit layout
- Host: Grok Build, ceremony tier `rapid`
- No `xbrief/active/` brief existed (see #4544), so `xbrief:preflight` had no declared scope to check against

## Why it matters

Directive's stay-on-task rules (#198, #241, skill exit conditions, intent ceiling in `contracts/intent-ceiling.md`) are about not drifting into adjacent work. A literal scope-limit sentence in the operator's own prompt is the strongest possible signal of where the boundary is, and it wasn't honored. Full CRUD is a reasonable default for an unconstrained build; it's out of scope for this one.

Small drift here, but the same behaviour on a larger brief is exactly what the framework exists to prevent.

## Suggested direction

- When the operator prompt contains an explicit scope-limit phrase ("only", "do not add", "nothing beyond", "initial version only"), the Implementation Intent Gate (#810) should record it as a hard ceiling on the seeded brief, and pre-PR should diff shipped surface (routes / actions / pages) against the requirement list, warn-first.
- Cheapest first ship (per #3265): one check that lists exported server actions / route files not traceable to a requirement line, with a single remediation string ("remove, or add to the brief and get operator approval").
